title: SHE CHOSE SIDES.
paragraphs: SHE CHOSE SIDES.

Two men stood on her roof.
The king’s soldiers were pounding on the door.
And the woman hiding them?
A prostitute.

Not a prophet.
Not a priest.
Not a princess.
A woman whose reputation clung to her like the dust of Jericho’s streets.
Yet that night… heaven was watching.

The spies from Israel had slipped into Jericho quietly.
But the city had already heard the rumors.

A sea split in two.
Kings crushed in battle.
A God who fought for His people.
Fear spread through the city like wildfire.
Rahab felt it too.
But while everyone else trembled…
She believed.
When the king’s men came searching, Rahab did the unthinkable.
She hid the spies under stalks of flax on her roof.
Then she faced the soldiers and sent them chasing ghosts into the night.
One choice.
One risk.
One moment where she chose the God she had never seen over the king she lived under.
Later that night she whispered to the spies:

“The LORD your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath.”
—Joshua 2:11
Think about that.
A pagan woman in a corrupt city made one of the clearest declarations of faith in the entire Old Testament.
She had heard the stories.
And she believed.
But Rahab didn’t just believe quietly.
She chose sides.
Faith is never neutral.
You cannot hide spies for the people of God and remain loyal to the kingdom of darkness.
The spies gave her a sign.
A scarlet cord.

Tie it in your window, they said.
When judgment comes, anyone inside your house will live.
And when Jericho’s walls collapsed…
Rahab’s house still stood.
Grace hanging from the window.
Red as blood.
But here’s the twist that shakes history.
Rahab didn’t just survive.
She was welcomed into Israel.
She married into the people of God.
And centuries later…
Her name appeared in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.
Yes.

The prostitute from Jericho became an ancestor of the Savior of the world.
(Matthew 1:5)
This is the Gospel written in advance.

A scarlet cord in a window.
A coming judgment.
A shelter for anyone who believes.
Just like the blood of Jesus.
Maybe your past looks like Jericho.
Maybe your name carries shame.
Maybe people know your worst chapter.
Rahab proves something powerful:

God is not looking for perfect people.
He is looking for people who will choose His side.
When you trust Christ, your past does not disqualify you.
Grace rewrites your lineage.
So today the question is simple.
When the moment comes…
Which side will you choose?
Because one decision of faith can change not only your story—
but generations after you.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
